caption_text_source.note: YouTube advertises a zh-TW track without the ASR flag on the original 2026 watch page. The archived metadata identifies the same video and source VTT by ID and language. topic_alignment.paraphrase: Lee names the TTT paper. At 2764.061 he revisits an RNN update; h holds the state, and the recurrent maps update it and produce the output. From 2806.737 through 2831.995 he reinterprets the state as fast parameters theta and the maps as meta-parameters phi. The 2830-second frame shows the recurrence and both sets of dotted arrows.

Lee points to the previous year’s fourth lecture for an explanation of the relationships among RNNs, Transformers and Mamba. The 2860-second frame shows the Mamba and robot illustration also found on p.52.

Lee names Titans and Nested Learning. From 2892.856 he describes an interpretation in which a changing memory or attention is treated as a parameter and other network parameters govern how it changes. The 2880-second frame shows the two studies, with the Titans memory diagram above the Nested Learning schematic.

Lee asks what learning means, proposing that it changes behavior. He evokes changes in human neural connections and, at 2942.806 seconds, contrasts them with the familiar account of changing a machine-learning model’s parameters. The 2930-second frame shows the parallel rows of brains and networks.

Lee changes the analogy: the state or attention during inference plays the role of changing neural activity/connections, and the trained network parameters correspond to genes. At 3114.911 seconds he gives the example of changing behavior by supplying new rules in the context. The 3040-second frame shows the brain and DNA symbols. The next physical page, p.56, starts a distinct discussion of more than two timescales at 3142.105 seconds.
